_comment: pi-py server security policy. Loaded via PI_POLICY; see src/pi/security/policy.py.
Both compose files bind-mount this file to /etc/pi-py/policy.json; the bare-metal
deployment points PI_POLICY at it directly. Keep ONE copy - drift between the two
would mean compose and bare-metal enforce different rules.
path_sandbox and redact are forced on by server_policy() even if omitted here.
deny_command_patterns are case-insensitive regexes matched with re.search (anywhere in the command).
The flag groups (-{1,2}[a-z-]+ )* accept long options too, so 'rm -rf --no-preserve-root /' is caught.
web_fetch/web_search are denied because they run INSIDE THE APP PROCESS, not in the
sandbox, so PI_SANDBOX=docker and --network none do not restrict them at all. web.py
does no URL validation and follows redirects, which makes them an open SSRF path to
the Volcano Engine metadata service (100.96.0.96 was confirmed reachable). Re-enable
only after web.py rejects private/link-local/metadata addresses AND re-validates every
The command patterns are the safety net for when bash is NOT sandboxed (PI_SANDBOX empty
runs it in the app process as whatever user the app is). They cannot stop secret theft:
env, printenv, set, /proc/self/environ and any interpreter one-liner all read the same
environment. Only running bash in a container closes that.
